title: Innovation Accounting
equation: Innovation Score = Cohort Behavior × Conversion × Retention
hook: Downloads going up while nobody sticks around isn't growth. It's a leaky bucket with good marketing.
statement: Track progress with numbers that show whether your business model is actually working.
explainer: Total signups can rise while the business quietly dies. Grouping users by when they joined, called cohorts, shows whether each new group engages, pays, and sticks better than the last.
sop: Drop vanity numbers like raw downloads and page views.
Group users into cohorts by the month they started.
Track each cohort's activation, conversion, and retention.
Set milestones that mean real progress.
Pivot when the cohort numbers stall.
equation_example: Cohort Behavior 60%, Conversion 20%, Retention 45%. 0.60 × 0.20 × 0.45 = 0.054, about 5.4%. Higher means engaged users convert and stick around. Lower means your growth numbers are hiding a leaky core.
question: Pick your last two monthly cohorts and compare how many people from each are still around.
closing_statement: Rising engagement means little if it never converts.
